required_outcomes: Asks the landlord (Quinn) whether he approves sending a contractor to replace the conservatory back-door lock and supply new keys, describing the snapped key and that there is no spare.
Acknowledges the tenant's report and says the landlord's approval is being sought, without promising a visit date.
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant first whether the door can still be locked or whether part of the key is stuck in the lock, sent alongside the landlord request.
Offering the landlord the choice between the agency's contractor and his own locksmith in the same approval request.
Putting the case on hold for the landlord with a review date a few days out after sending the request.
positive_behaviours: Checks or states whether the agency holds a spare key for that door before asking the landlord.
Asks the tenant whether the door can still be secured, so a security risk would be spotted early.
Suggests in the approval request how many replacement keys are needed and who holds them.
red_flags: Escalating a routine lock and key repair to a human.
Treating the report as an emergency with no facts suggesting the property cannot be secured.
prohibited_actions: Instructing or assigning a locksmith before the landlord approves, when there is no spend limit, standing instruction or emergency on record.
Telling the tenant they will be charged for the repair or the new keys.
critical_failures: Ending the turn without asking the landlord for approval and without any message to the tenant, so the repair stalls at intake.
